Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year after record-breaking season for Man United... and he's one of just TWO stars outside Arsenal and Man City in the Team of the Year
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has been named the PFA Players' Player of the Year after a landmark 2025-26 campaign in which the Manchester United captain broke the Premier League record for most assists in a single season.

Fernandes surpassed the previous mark of 20, jointly held by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, on the final day of the season when he set up Patrick Dorgu's header against Brighton to register his 21st assist of the campaign.

Fernandes has already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick by collecting the prestigious, player-voted award at Manchester's Opera House on Tuesday evening.

He was United's first to claim the PFA Players' Player of the Year since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

'Winning this, being voted by the ones that every week go out on the pitch against me, is something that makes me very proud,' he said.

'Because they've been there, they're playing against me, they've seen what I'm capable of doing, and for them to vote for me is something I'm very grateful for.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was crowned PFA Player of the Year on Tuesday

Fernandes, who attended with his wife Ana, was also named in the PFA Team of the Year

Fernandes had already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick on Tuesday evening

'It's always nice to see the name of the club in these kinds of awards, and obviously the players stand out with the club behind them. That's very important for us.

'I hope that from now on we can have even more players from our club having this kind of recognition, because it's also important and means that we're doing something very good.

'Individually, you want to have these accolades to show that your game is helping the team and that there are a lot of good things you've been doing to help them.'

The Portugal midfielder was the sole United player to have been named in the PFA's Premier League Team of the Year, and he is joined by Brentford's Igor Thiago as the only other non-Manchester City or Arsenal player in the side.

David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice all made up a heavily defensive Arsenal contingent, while Nico O'Reilly, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland completed City's representation.

Mohamed Salah was named PFA Players' Player of the Year last year, but no Liverpool players made the cut this time.

O'Reilly also scooped the Men's Young Player of the Year award, beating team-mate Cherki as well as Max Dowman, Junior Kroupi, Kobbie Mainoo and Rio Ngumoha to the prize.

Elsewhere, Everton's Hayden Hackney was named the Championship Player of the Year after playing a key role in Middlesbrough's run to the play-off final in May. He signed for David Moyes' side in July after missing out on promotion with his boyhood club.

Nico O'Reilly (left) won the PFA Young Player, while Declan Rice was in the Team of the Year

Dom Ballard took home the League One title after a standout season for Leyton Orient while Swindon's Aaron Drinan won the League Two award.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award for the second time after also collecting it in 2024, becoming only the third player to win it twice after Lucy Bronze (2014 and 2017) and Fran Kirby (2018 and 2021).

Shaw was the WSL's Golden Boot winner last season, scoring 21 goals in 22 matches as she helped fire her team to the top-flight trophy for the first time in 10 years.

The other nominees for the top prize in the women's game were Manchester City team-mate Yui Hasegawa, Chelsea's Lauren James, Manchester United's Jess Park, Arsenal's Alessia Russo and Aston Villa's Kirsty Hanson.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award

Arsenal's Olivia Smith scooped the Young Player of the Year award after a fine season

PREMIER LEAGUE AND WSL TEAMS OF THE YEAR Premier League team of the year: David Raya (Arsenal); Jurrien Timber (Arsenal), William Saliba (Arsenal), Gabriel Magalhaes (Arsenal), Nico O'Reilly (Man City); Bruno Fernandes (Man United), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Rayan Cherki (Man City); Erling Haaland (Man City), Antoine Semenyo (Man City), Igor Thiago (Brentford). WSL team of the year: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea); Kerstin Casparij (Man City), Toko Koga (Tottenham), Ellie Carpenter (Chelsea), Emily Fox (Arsenal); Yui Hasegawa (Man City), Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal), Jess Park (Man United); Bunny Shaw (Man City), Alessia Russo (Arsenal), Lauren James (Chelsea).

Hannah Hampton, Kerstin Casparij, Toko Koga, Ellie Carpenter and Emily Fox made up the remainder of the PFA WSL Team of the Year.

Arsenal's Olivia Smith, the former most expensive transfer in women's history, scooped the Young Player of the Year award.

The 22-year-old Canada international became the first women's player to surpass the seven-figure barrier last summer when Arsenal signed her from Liverpool for £1 million, and had an impressive campaign, scoring five goals and recording three assists.

Sports.title: Serena Williams makes spectacular return to US Open as she teams up with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed power pairing... four years after stepping back from tennis at the Grand Slam
Sports.content:
Serena Williams made an emotional return to Flushing Meadows on Tuesday when she teamed up with Spanish sensation Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open's mixed doubles event.

The tennis icon, 44, continued her comeback tour, returning to the Grand Slam where she bowed out of the sport four years ago.

Williams announced that she would be 'evolving away' from tennis following the 2022 US Open. But, after returning to tennis's major stages at Wimbledon and the Cincinnati Open earlier this year, she stepped into the spotlight on Arthur Ashe once again.

The US Tennis Association announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz, 23, had been handed a wild card for the year's final Grand Slam.

The pair were granted entry into the star-studded 16-team field competing for a $1million prize, sealing a stunning return to the US Open for Williams.

They took to the iconic Arthur Ashe court on Tuesday afternoon, facing Lloyd Glasspool and Erin Routliffe in the first round of the event.

Serena Williams made an emotional return to the US Open in the mixed doubles on Tuesday

The 44-year-old teamed up with Spanish ace Carlos Alcaraz (pictured) in the event

The tennis legend stepped back from the sport following the 2022 US Open

It will be the 44-year-old's first time playing at the US Open since 2022. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion returned to tennis earlier this summer.

But she is not planning to play singles in New York. The USTA had been holding one women's wild card - presumably in case Williams wanted it. On Saturday, however, organizers announced it had gone to American Sofia Kenin , the 2020 Australian Open champion.

Williams played singles at Wimbledon, losing in the first round and sustaining a knee injury, before teaming up with older sister Venus to play doubles at the Cincinnati Open. In their first match together since the 2022 US Open, the sisters were beaten by Peyton Stearns and Marta Kostyuk, 6-2, 1-6, 10-8.

Serena Williams has won a US Open mixed doubles title before, taking the crown in 1998 alongside Max Mirnyi, who now works with Aryna Sabalenka . Nearly three decades on, the competition is now a star-studded, two-day competition, with Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic among the other big names taking part this year.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, announced this week he would return to defend his US Open singles title after being sidelined since April with a right wrist injury.

News of his comeback - and his partnership with Williams - is a huge boost for fans after rival Jannik Sinner pulled out.

The world No 1 announced on Friday that he will miss the US Open with a knee injury.

In a statement on social media, the Italian wrote: 'Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year.

Serena Williams was world No.1 in singles the day Carlos Alcaraz was born.



23 years later, the two join forces in Grand Slam mixed doubles! pic.twitter.com/MvUSxZXlyf — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 25, 2026

The tennis icon continued her comeback tour, returning to the Grand Slam in New York

Serena Williams' Wimbledon singles comeback came to an early end on Tuesday

The legend was supported by her husband Alexis Ohanian and their two daughters

'We have been back on court in Monte Carlo over the last couple of days and have realised that I still need more time to recover from my right knee issue.

'I'm obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart. I was very much looking forward to coming back and playing in the electric atmosphere in front of the great fans there.'

Sinner turned pro in 2018 and has never missed a Grand Slam tournament in his entire career, winning five in total - including the US Open two years ago and Wimbledon this summer.

The 25-year-old has been dominant so far in 2026, winning the first five ATP Masters 1000 events, two of which in the US in Indian Wells and Miami.

After crashing out of Wimbledon in the first round and suffering a similar fate alongside sister Venus in the women's doubles in Cincinnati, many have questioned if Williams still possesses her titan talent.

Others may be more focused on the question mark over one particular detail of her preparation -whether Williams has continued to use GLP-1 jabs managed by telehealth company Ro, of which she became a vocal paid spokesperson for last year.

Williams returned to tennis this summer and played with sister Venus at the Cincinnati Open

The seven-time Wimbledon champion's husband Alexis Ohanian sits on the company's board and was an early investor. As recently as this February Williams, the company's celebrity face, featured in a Super Bowl advert for the brand and its Zepbound tirzepatide jab, which is also marketed under the name Mounjaro.

Williams, who is said to have lost close to two and a half stone, or 34 pounds (15kg) using the drug, previously called her challenge to lose weight following the birth of her two children 'the one opponent (she) couldn't beat'.

It remains unclear as to whether Williams has continued to use the drug, which also treats symptoms of diabetes, with her publicist declining to comment when asked by the Atlantic.

But although GLP-1s are not banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), they are one of the drugs under ongoing investigation as to whether they might be classed as performance-enhancing in the future.

Sports.title: Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson
Sports.content:
Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have agreed a staggering £50million sale Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest.

Delap is now in line to leave Stamford Bridge after only a single season, with the Blues having triggered his £30m release clause at Ipswich Town last summer.

He scored one Premier League goal in 28 games in 2025-26, and two in 41 in all competitions.

Delap was missing from the Chelsea squad which defeated Fulham 3-2 in their first Premier League fixture of the season.

The 23-year-old had been training separately to Xabi Alonso’s main group at their Cobham base after being made available for sale, along with Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson is also closing in on a £65m switch to Aston Villa. That would see Chelsea secure their asking price for the 25-year-old Senegalese.

Chelsea have agreed a £50million fee with Nottingham Forest to sell them Liam Delap

Nicolas Jackson is also nearing a £65million move to Aston Villa from Chelsea

The Chelsea star is understood to be keen on a reunion with former boss Unai Emery

They had been seeking at least £50m for Delap. It is believed Forest’s agreement involves £45m plus £5m in add-ons.

It represents a remarkable profit secured by Chelsea after a disappointing campaign for Delap, whose No 9 shirt was handed to Joao Pedro before this current season started.

Delap had been keen to stay at Chelsea and prove himself, but he became surplus this summer.

With Joao Pedro untouchable at the front of Chelsea's attack, they also signed Danny Welbeck from Brighton and have Emmanuel Emegha. Jackson and Marc Guiu are in line to leave.

Sports.title: Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Bruno Fernandes is joined by WAG as Declan Rice leads FIVE Arsenal players in attendance with football world descending on Manchester for bash
Sports.content:
Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Bruno Fernandes is joined by WAG as Declan Rice leads FIVE Arsenal players in attendance with football world descending on Manchester for bash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A plethora of key figures within English football have all descended upon Manchester ahead of Tuesday night's Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Awards.

The annual ceremony is taking place this year at the Opera House Theatre.

Among those in attendance sees representation from several Premier League teams.

Champions Arsenal are represented by a key quintet of David Raya, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes, William Saliba and Declan Rice. Those five will hope to be involved in at least the PFA Team of the Year, while potentially collecting the prize for PFA Player of the Year.

Arsenal were in a title pursuit with Manchester City all of last season and beat them in the Community Shield two Sundays ago.

That quintet will cross paths with City trio Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki and Nico O'Reilly who are also there.

Arsenal stars David Raya, Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba (left to right) were on the red carpet ahead of the PFA Awards in Manchester on Tuesday night

Manchester City were represented at the bash by Antoine Semenyo (centre) and Rayan Cherki

Semenyo enjoyed a prolific season at Bournemouth and City last term, while O'Reilly had a breakout campaign which saw him end it as part of England head coach Thomas Tuchel's - who is also attending - World Cup squad which reached the semi-finals.

Aged just 21, the City academy graduate is the favourite to win PFA Young Player of the Year.

City's bitter rivals Manchester United are represented by head coach Michael Carrick, CEO Omar Berrada and Bruno Fernandes.

The pair have had a busy day following the £70million transfer completion of Carlos Baleba from Brighton and Hove Albion.

Baleba will add some much-needed dynamism to United's midfield and will play behind captain Fernandes - who is another leading contender for the PFA Player of the Year award after a fantastic 2025-26 where he broke the Premier League assists record for a single season with 21.

In May, he won the Football Writers' Association's men's Footballer of the Year award and was named Premier League player of the season, meaning it could be a clean sweep of accolades if he's victorious come 9pm.

Liverpool icon Kenny Dalglish also donned the red carpet alongside his wife Marina.

Arsenal are also well represented in the women's game in Manchester with Alessia Russo, Mariona Caldentey, Emily Fox and Olivia Smith representing the Gunners too.

Nico O'Reilly (left) could win PFA Young Player, in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel there

Bruno Fernandes registered a record-breaking 21 assists in the Premier League last season

Michael Carrick (left) and Omar Berrada are among those representing Manchester United

Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish smiles for the cameras alongside his wife Marina

Arsenal Women's Olivia Smith, Mariona Caldentey, Alessia Russo, and Emily Fox (left-right) attended Tuesday's event at the Manchester Opera Theatre

Former Lionesses Karen Carney, Eni Aluko, Jordan Nobbs and Toni Duggan are also in the crowd for Tuesday night's showpiece.

In terms of former male footballers the likes of Mikael Silvestre, Sebastian Bassong, Ashley Young, Asmir Begovic, Kolo Toure are also present.

Ex-Manchester United and Arsenal defender Silvestre hit the headlines on Monday after calling out FIFA president Gianni Infantino, telling him to stand down.

Silvestre, who is part of FIFA's Players' Voice Panel, took to X to demand change, writing: 'Enough is enough!'

The post, which went on to call for structural change within FIFA, was shared by France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit as well as Lioness Lucy Bronze.

Infantino is also facing calls to quit from his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in the wake of a hugely controversial plan to sell stakes in a company to run the World Cup to private investors.

And players have now begun to speak out against the 56-year-old, with Monday's widely shared statement evidential of those who 'share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world'.

Karen Carney (left) and Mikael Silvestre are among the ex-footballers at Tuesday's ceremony

It added: 'Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA's current leadership.

'For too long we've seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

'Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership's ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football.'

Silvestre's interjection is significant given it effectively comes from within the FIFA fold, with the Players' Voice Panel a 16-strong group formed by the global governing body to monitor and advise on initiatives to tackle racism.

The statement continued: 'Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.

'We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future of our sport.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
